title: AI and machine learning in network operations

cards.heading: AI and machine learning
cards.body: Artificial intelligence is the broad field of systems that perform tasks needing human-like judgement. Machine learning (ML) is the part that learns patterns from data instead of following hand-written rules. Supervised learning trains on labelled examples; unsupervised learning finds structure and anomalies in unlabelled data.

cards.heading: Where it helps operations
cards.body: Anomaly detection spots behaviour that departs from a learned baseline (unusual traffic, rising errors). Predictive analytics forecasts failures and capacity needs before they hurt. Correlation reduces thousands of alerts to a probable root cause. Platforms such as Catalyst Center assurance apply these to telemetry.

cards.heading: Generative AI
cards.body: Large language models can draft configurations, explain logs and answer troubleshooting questions in plain language. They can also be confidently wrong, so a human must review anything before it touches production, and sensitive data shouldn't be pasted into public services.
